abstract: In online product search, returned alternatives often look alike. We investigate when a product's visual separation from its closest look-alike in a returned set increases its choice probability. We introduce two occasion-level constructs: contextual visual distinctiveness (image distance from the nearest similar alternative in the consideration set) and relative fit (compatibility with the search query). We hypothesize that distinctiveness favors selection and is highly contextual, yields a premium that rises with relative fit, and matters most when text descriptions fail to differentiate options. Analyzing over 800,000 e-commerce search events using dense representations, we apply search-event and product fixed effects to evaluate the exact same product alongside varying visual neighbors. Results show a product is significantly more likely to be clicked when it lacks a close look-alike. This distinctiveness premium increases with relative fit and roughly doubles when competing descriptions are highly similar. Consistent with a model where distinctiveness aids in standing out pre-evaluation rather than increasing inherent utility, the extra clicks distinctiveness recruits convert 5-7% less often downstream. Ultimately, the evidence characterizes visual differentiation as a local attention allocation mechanism whose value depends on query fit and information from competing cues.

ob.tldr: 研究电商搜索中产品视觉独特性对选择的影响。基于80万次搜索事件，利用密集表示与搜索事件及产品固定效应，发现缺乏近似外观的产品点击率显著更高，该独特性溢价随相对契合度上升而增强，并在竞品描述高度相似时约翻倍。但独特性吸引的额外点击后续转化率低5-7%，表明视觉差异化是搜索前注意分配机制，而非提升产品内在效用。

title: Contextual Visual Distinctiveness in Online Product Search
title_zh: 在线产品搜索中的情境视觉显著性
